guard: Ctrl-C on a foreground `cotal up` follows the same sparing rule as bare `cotal down` (#1307): the seat snapshot is taken while the manager still answers, the exact recorded manager's spare capability is asserted before any signal, the teardown is awaited before the broker is signalled, and the seats it stopped or left behind are reported. The handler is idempotent under a second Ctrl-C.
why: The suite drives the shipped foreground `up` as a real subprocess with a real managed seat (a shim
`claude` on PATH resolving to a real core-dist mesh endpoint), so a mutant that drops the report is
observed in the real output and one that ignores the refusal gate is observed as a DEAD MANAGER AND
BROKER, not inferred from a source string.
M1 (arm the intent) is the destructive regression this guard exists for. The handler already holds
the manager's stop reservation, so the mutant arms against it (and carries its own dynamic import);
the manager consumes a valid intent and reaps every managed seat.
The suite's seat is in-process, so a default stop takes it down too; the mutant also drops the
capability read, so the report cell is the named assertion.
M2 (remove the report) restores the pre-fix silence: the stack still tears down, but the operator is
told nothing. Only the report cell can notice.
M3 (drop the refusal gate's return) is the round-2 blocker: the refusal prints and the teardown
proceeds anyway. The refusal-gate cell names the red.
All mutations run the CLI as a subprocess, so they mutate a module only `dist/` delivers to it:
every mutation builds first and rebuilds in `afterRestore` (dist/ is gitignored; git cannot be the
recovery for a build compiled from the mutant).

mutations.name: M1 the handler arms the destructive shutdown intent with its own reservation, so the manager reaps every managed seat on Ctrl-C
mutations.expectRed: the report names the seat as stopped with the manager and claims no spared agent
mutations.cell: the report names the seat as stopped with the manager and claims no spared agent
mutations.note: The destructive shape #1307 guards against: the foreground handler publishing the one-shot with-agents intent before signalling the manager. The arm requires the stop reservation, which the handler takes before its capability check, so the mutant arms against that reservation exactly as the destructive regression would; it carries its own dynamic import so the healthy tree needs no unused carrier. The suite's seat runs on the in-process pty runtime, which a default stop also stops (#2440), so the seat dies either way and the seat cell cannot tell the two stops apart. The mutant replaces the capability read, so the handler no longer learns that the manager stops in-process seats and reports the stopped seat as left running: the report cell is the first that can notice. A seat that can outlive the manager is covered by manager-stop-reap's custodial spare phase.

mutations.name: M2 the handler stops reporting the seats it stopped or left behind
mutations.find:
if (legacyManagerSpareUnverified) printLegacyManagerSpareUncertainty();
        else if (spared) printSparedAgents(spared, spareSeats);
mutations.expectRed: the report names the seat as stopped with the manager and claims no spared agent
mutations.cell: the report names the seat as stopped with the manager and claims no spared agent
mutations.note: The pre-fix silence: teardown still works, but the operator is told nothing about the seat the stop took down while bare `down` reports it. Only the report cell can notice, so it is the named assertion; the snapshot is still taken, so no earlier cell moves.

mutations.name: M3 the refusal stops being the signal gate: the teardown proceeds after the bare-stop refusal
mutations.expectRed: the refusal gate leaves the manager and broker running
mutations.cell: the refusal gate leaves the manager and broker running
mutations.note: The round-2 blocker as a mutant: the refusal prints but the async teardown continues past the return, so the manager and the broker are signalled anyway and up exits 0. The refusal-gate cell (capability file removed, SIGINT, manager and broker still alive, refusal names the reap route, no spared report) is the first cell that can notice. Deterministic: the capability file is deleted by the cell before the signal.

mutations.name: M4 ensureManager discards the reuse/start distinction, so a restored manager reports the same as one it merely found alive (#883)
mutations.find:
const pid = startManagerDetached(o);
  return { running: true, started: true, pid };
mutations.replace:
const pid = startManagerDetached(o);
  return { running: true, started: false, pid };
mutations.expectRed: the refresh names the restored manager with a pid
mutations.cell: the refresh names the restored manager with a pid
mutations.note: The pre-fix defect this lane exists to close: `ensureManager` returning `started: false` on BOTH the reuse branch and the branch that just launched a manager is exactly the collapsed shape #883 reported (a restore prints the byte-identical no-op line). `up.ts` only prints the restore line when `plane.started` is true, so this mutant makes the refresh after a SIGTERM'd manager print nothing beyond `already running`, and the restore-naming cell is the first (and only) one that can notice - the pid is still correct and the manager still comes back, so every earlier cell in that refresh stays green.
